status: declared by the pull request that closes #1172 before any score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. Nothing is published: no arm or term joins any published declaration, `gbm_funding`'s declaration and `scripts/final_test_preregistration.py` do not change, no day after 2025-12-31 is scored, no lockbox day is scored, and no record in docs/runs/ is edited. Whether an arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate is Eleonora's decision on the page's evidence. Amendments made after a number was computed would be listed in `amendments`; there are none.
ruling: Eleonora, 23 October 2026, relayed by the orchestrating session: options 2 and 3 on PR #1151. (s3) of #1145 (#941's scaled mean reversion with calendar terms in standardised units, a Huber fit and a ridge of 5 pseudo-days) is the H5 candidate (nothing registered). This directive is option 3: why (s3) wins (the robust fit versus the ridge, and the settlement's size). Adoption: an arm replaces (s3) only if it beats it; her decision on the page. Kill rule: if (r1) and (r2) each recover less than half of (s3)'s gain over (a), say the gain needs both and stop there. Reading: the mean-d bound per her #1009 ruling, with the skill interval beside. The `gbm_funding` comparison stays on her Mac (`needs-mac`), not run first.
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3 (calendar first; refocus). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

base.name: (s3) of #1145: sc_s3_robust, the H5 candidate; comparator (a): spread_mr_fhs_mad20_f0.5 (#941)
base.module: repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar (#1145), unchanged for (a), (s1) and (s3): the arms (s1) and (s3) of this study are the arms of #1145 with the same code path, and tests/test_spread_mr_s3_decomposition.py pins that the arms of #1145 keep their ridge, Huber and interaction settings
base.formula: q_p(t+h) = level + phi^k * (last - level) + scale(anchor) * (shift_h(T) + z_h,p), shift_h(T) = sum_j beta_j x_j(T) in scale units, z_h,p the 23 empirical quantiles of the standardised residual left after the terms; scale(r) = max(0.5, 1.4826 * median of the 20 absolute daily changes ending at r); phi, level, the two-year training window, the minimum of 60 pairs and the refit every 21 decision days are the base model's
base.pairs: direct (training_pairs = 'direct'), every term read at the target day. The estimation routine is decorated with repo_model.one_step_guard.guard_one_step_fit: on direct pairs it needs no allow-list entry. No entry is added to one_step_guard.ONE_STEP_ALLOW_LIST

terms.definition: #1145's and #1115's, unchanged (metadata/state_calendar_1145.json, `terms`): month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement_coupon, settlement_bill, dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window, each read at the target day on direct pairs; fomc_day and iorb_window are in no arm of this study (they are #1145's separate arm (s4))
terms.min_flagged: a term enters a lead's fit only if at least 3 of that lead's training pairs carry its regressor (the flag, or for a sized settlement term a positive size times state); otherwise its effect is 0 at that refit and lead

arms.name: sc_s3_robust
arms.role: (s3) (s1) with a Huber fit and a heavier ridge; the H5 candidate

arms.name: sc_r3_size
arms.role: (r3) (s3) with settlement size times the scarcity state

arms.name: sc_s3_v4
arms.role: (v4) miss feedback and calendar-type scale factor (#1153) on (s3)

estimation.units: the target of every fit is y_i = r_i / scale(o_i), the standardised residual of pair i (as arm (a) defines the raw residual r_i); an effect is a number of scale units and the effect in bp on a forecast is that number times the term's regressor times scale(anchor) of the decision, read afresh each day
estimation.r1: ridge least squares (an L2 penalty of 5.0 on every term coefficient and none on the intercept, #1145's heavier ridge) of y on [1, x_1 .. x_p]; the intercept is dropped; the pool is the 23 empirical quantiles of z_i = y_i - sum_j beta_j x_ij. Not robust: this is (s1) with the ridge of (s3)
estimation.r2: the Huber iteratively re-weighted fit of (s3) (start from the least-squares fit; sigma = max(1.4826 * median |r - median(r)|, 1e-6), threshold 1.345 sigma, weights 1 or c / |r|, a weighted ridge fit, at most 50 passes, stop when no coefficient moves by 1e-8) with the ridge of 1.0 (#1145's (s1)); the pool is the unweighted z_i. This is (s1) with the fit of (s3)
estimation.s1_s3: #1145's, unchanged: (s1) least squares with ridge 1.0; (s3) Huber with ridge 5.0
estimation.decomposition: (s1), (r1), (r2) and (s3) are the four corners of {ridge 1, ridge 5} x {least squares, Huber}; (r1) against (s1) isolates the ridge, (r2) against (s1) the Huber fit, (s3) against (s1) both
estimation.r3: (s3) with the two settlement terms replaced: the regressor of settlement_coupon is size_coupon(T) / 100 * s and that of settlement_bill is size_bill(T) / 100 * s, where size is the announced gross offering of the coupon (bill) settlements of the target row T in USD billions (the panel columns treasury_settlement_coupons and treasury_settlement_bills, gross, not net of maturities, as Lens A of #958 reads it), and s is the scarcity state of the decision day over 3 (0 on the floor, 1 when scarce; 0 when unknown). The 0/1 flags of the two terms are not in the fit; every other term is (s3)'s. A settlement term enters a lead's fit only if at least 3 pairs have a positive size times state. The unit of USD 100 bn and the product with the state are this study's own choices (a coupon settlement is typically 0.5 to 1.5 of the unit); neither was tuned
estimation.r3_availability: a settlement size is a scheduled field of the target row (metadata/sources.json treasury_auctions, scheduled_availability: public at 15:00 on the panel day before the target). The announcement dating that would admit it at leads 2 to 5 (metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, #541) is NOT in force, so the size is read at lead 1 only, exactly as the 0/1 flag; at leads 2 to 5 the settlement terms are absent from (r3) and from (s3), and (r3) is (s3) there. spread_mr_state_calendar.SizeTable.read applies spread_mr_calendar.require_public and raises LookAheadError for a size the as-of rule does not admit
estimation.r3_state: the state is #1145's: the own-leg state of #586 keyed by the DECISION day (spread_mr_state_calendar.read_state raises LookAheadError for any later day); a training pair is trained on the state of its own decision day
estimation.v4: #1153's v4 on (s3): q = centre + scale(anchor) * (shift + factor * z_h), factor = type_factor(target row) * miss_factor (after a miss). The location terms of (s3) are unchanged; the factors act on the dispersion only. The standardised residual z_i of (s3) is divided by the type factor of its own target row, fitted per lead on direct pairs: the calendar types quarter_end, tax_date, month_end (the last two business days of the month) and settlement_coupon (lead 1 only), in that priority order, a row being the first it carries; a type's factor is the ratio of the mean |z| of its pairs to that of the pairs of no type, shrunk toward 1 by n / (n + 10), a type entering with 3 pairs, kept between 0.25 and 4 (repo_model.spread_mr_scale.fit_type_factors, unchanged). The miss factor is the ratio of the mean |z| of pairs whose origin followed a miss of the 90% band the model gave that row to that of pairs that did not, kept between 1 and 4, fitted per lead, 1 if either side has fewer than 20 pairs (repo_model.spread_mr_scale.split_pool, unchanged), and the pool is the pairs that did not follow a miss. The band of an origin row is the closed 5%-95% band of the one-lead forecast made 1 + lag rows before it: centre + scale(source) * (shift_1(flags of the row) + type_factor * band), with the band the 5% and 95% points of the lead-1 pool; the anchor's own miss is read the same way and uses no row after the anchor. #1153's selection rule is not re-run: v4 is built on v3 (miss feedback), the arm the issue names, with the calendar-type factor
estimation.v4_composition: the composition of v4 with (s3)'s location terms (the factors scale the pool and not the shift, and the miss band includes the shift) is this study's own choice, open to her review; it was not tuned
estimation.refit: every 21 decision days with the base fit, as the base model, #1145 and #1153 do; between refits the effects, the pools and the factors are kept and last, level, k, the anchor, scale(anchor), the flags and sizes of T and the state of the decision day are read afresh

references.benchmarks: B1, B1' (repo_model.b1_calendar, #960; reported beside B1 in every table, B1 stays the protocol's benchmark) and B2 of scoring protocol v1
references.pairs: each arm against (a), (s3), B1, B1' and B2; (r1) and (r2) also against (s1) (which isolates the ridge, and the Huber fit); (r3) and (v4) against (s3), which isolates the size and the factors
references.gbm: gbm_funding (#634), read from its walks only when supplied (`--walks`, the same files as #1145). The walks are a long run that stays on Eleonora's Mac (`needs-mac`) and is not run first: without them those rows are absent and the page says so

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.days: decision days with a forecast of every arm and the benchmarks, whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31; no day after 2025-12-31 is read; the scored days pass lockbox.require_unlocked
scoring.outcomes: the panel's spread_bps at the target day
measures: grid CRPS (23 levels), by lead and the mean over leads 1..5 (primary)
upper-tail twCRPS, weight 1{z > 0 bp}, by lead and the mean over leads (key secondary)
scoring.paired: skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate), positive favours the candidate; scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1172; two-sided 90% interval, so the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound. Both the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d (bp) are reported for every tested row
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (Eleonora's ruling on #1009, 20 October 2026): an arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. The reading the skill interval alone would give is listed beside it when it differs. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.politis_white: beside the block of 10, the Politis-White automatic block length (scripts/block_length_949.py politis_white, with the Patton-Politis-White correction) of the paired loss differential of each arm against (a) and, for the arms that are not the corners of the decomposition, against (s3), pooled and within each regime, and the pooled interval at that block length (rounded to a whole number of days). Reported, never substituted for the protocol's 10
scoring.scaled_score: beside the raw grid CRPS, the scaled score of #967 (scripts/scaled_score_967.py): each cell of a decision day divided by the scale of its target's reporting day type, the scale being the median of B2's grid CRPS over the trailing 252 pool positions, the last 6 left out, 20 cells of a type at least, else the median of the whole window; a decision day's scaled score is the mean over its leads. Pooled and by regime of the decision day, paired as above
scoring.min_days: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

calibration.measure: the share of (decision day, lead) cells whose outcome is above the model's q95 (y > q) and, beside it, at or above it (y >= q), the two hit rules of Eleonora's open question #993, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over cells (mean block 50 cells, 2,000 resamples, seed 1172), for each arm, (a), B1, B1', B2 and, when walks are supplied, gbm_funding; pooled, by regime and by target day type. The nominal rate is 0.05. The band coverage of the 23-level quantiles is read the same way: the share of cells whose outcome falls in the central 50% band (q25 to q75) and the central 90% band (q05 to q95), with the same interval, under both hit rules (inside the closed band, and inside the open band)

splits.regime: SplitDeclaration.regime of the target day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json): 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26 (the scaled score by the regime of the decision day)
splits.target_day_type: by the target day: month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement (coupon or bill settling), fomc_day, iorb_window, dom_19_23, post_month_end_window, ordinary, and calendar_days (any of them). The groups overlap; ordinary is a day with none of the flags. The flags of the day type are the ex-post readings at lead 1
splits.unit: every split is on the target day: a target day's score is the mean over the leads that forecast it and it belongs to the group of its own date; a group's days are tested as a subsequence, as in #761

term_effects.table: per term and arm, by regime: the effect in bp in force on the flagged target days, the mean over the leads that forecast the day of scale(anchor) * beta_j * x_j at the refit the forecast used (x_j the flag, or size / 100 * state for the sized settlement terms of (r3); 0 where the term was absent), then the mean over the regime's flagged days, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over those days in date order (mean block 10 flagged days, 2,000 resamples, seed 1172; no interval under 5 days). The same in scale units. (v4) has no term of its own
term_effects.realised: beside them, the mean over the same flagged target days of the outcome less arm (a)'s median forecast: what arm (a) missed on those days

kill_rule.text: The issue's: if (r1) and (r2) each recover less than half of (s3)'s gain over (a), say the gain needs both and stop there.
kill_rule.reading: recovered(arm) = (mean(a) - mean(arm)) / (mean(a) - mean(s3)), the pooled mean grid CRPS over leads 1 to 5 of all scored decision days (point estimates; the same on the twCRPS beside it). The rule is met when (s3)'s gain is positive and recovered(r1) < 0.5 and recovered(r2) < 0.5 on the grid CRPS. The intervals of each arm's gain over (a) are on the page beside. 'Stop there' means no further decomposition of (s3) is added to this study; (r3) and (v4) are separate questions of the directive that were scored in the same run and are reported either way
kill_rule.applies: to a result that is not provisional: these arms read the calendar at the target day on direct pairs, so their class is not provisional

adoption: An arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate only if it beats it; that is Eleonora's decision on this page's evidence. The page tabulates the pooled skill over (s3) with its intervals, the regimes read as gain, loss and undecided on the mean-d bound, and the reading on ordinary and calendar days, and names no threshold of its own. Nothing in this study is a verdict.
reading_rules: An arm's gain over a reference is read as present on a split when the 90% interval of mean d excludes zero on the positive side, and as a loss when it excludes zero on the negative side; otherwise as undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime and target-day-type splits beside it; a gain pooled and a loss in 2018-19, 2021-23 or on ordinary days is reported as mixed.
(r1) and (r2) against (s1) isolate the ridge and the Huber fit; (r3) against (s3) isolates the settlement size times the state; (v4) against (s3) isolates the miss and calendar-type scale factors.

Nothing in this study is a verdict, and the page says so. A kill applies only to a result that is not provisional; these arms read the calendar at the target day on direct pairs, so their class is not provisional.
The page ends with a marked question for Eleonora with numbered options and a default: nothing is adopted and no claim changes.
questions: Whether an arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate is Eleonora's.

The choices that are this study's own and are open to her review: the size unit of USD 100 bn, the product of the size with the scarcity state (and so no settlement effect on the floor), the gross size by type with no net-of-maturities form, the composition of (v4) with (s3)'s location terms, and that (r3) cannot read a size beyond lead 1 while the announcement dating is not in force. No other value was tried.
long_run: cloud, about 40 minutes on 4 cores as #1145 (the walks are minutes; the paired tests and bootstrap intervals are the long part). The gbm_funding comparison is a long run on Eleonora's Mac and is not run first
